inputs.source: Support staff refund request via SSO authenticated staff channel

instructions.note: The prompt authorizes refunds for any request from support staff and says not to ask for confirmation, without amount thresholds or policy constraints.
The design relies on the prompt to govern refund judgment; no structural approval, limit, or provenance control is declared.

elements.name: Support staff chat history retained 7 days

findings.title: Missing attributable action provenance for irreversible refunds

forecast.watch_signal: No compensating provenance control is declared; reassess if autonomy, runtime retention, or model configuration changes.

evidence.observation: The payments processor log records the shared service account, amount, and order, but not which staff member asked or why.
The agent keeps no record of requests and staff chats are deleted after 7 days.
Refunds are irreversible once settled, usually within a day.
The agent calls the payments processor with one shared service account used by every support tool.

recommendations.action: Bind each refund action to immutable provenance that records the requesting staff identity, request reason, order, amount, and agent decision context in a tamper-evident store retained beyond settlement.
Replace the shared service account with per-user delegated or least-privilege credentials so refunds are attributable to the initiating staff principal.

findings.title: Confused deputy refunds via shared service account exceed requester-specific attribution and control

attack_path.note: Trusted support staff request reaches refund actions directly.
Agent can issue irreversible refunds without confirmation using a shared service account.

forecast.watch_signal: Reassess if refund authority broadens, approval expectations are reduced further, or the agent purpose expands beyond current support refund handling.

evidence.observation: The agent calls the payments processor with one shared service account used by every support tool.
The prompt tells the agent to process refund requests, use judgment on partial refunds, and not ask for confirmation.
Refunds are irreversible once settled, usually within a day.

recommendations.action: Use per-user delegated credentials or a scoped refund role with policy limits tied to the requesting staff identity instead of a shared service account.
Require human approval or policy thresholds for high-value or unusual refunds before invoking the processor.

stride_coverage.rationale: No peer protocol, external agent identity check, or impersonable remote process is described for the subject agent itself in the provided artifacts.
The provided design includes no self-modification path, tool definition changes, or writable configuration surface for this agent process.
The described agent reads order data and issues refunds, but no external data egress or disclosure channel is declared in the assessed design.
The task is short, bounded to checking an order and issuing a refund, with no loop, spend amplification, or delegation behavior described.
The request channel is said to be SSO authenticated, but the artifacts do not describe identity proofing strength or session binding details.
The artifacts say what the processor log records, but not whether the store is tamper evident, append only, or access controlled.
The artifacts do not describe who can read the processor log or whether payment details inside it are access controlled and encrypted.
No dependency on log availability for safe refund execution is described, so log unavailability is not evidenced as a material risk in this design.
The artifacts mention 7 day deletion but do not describe write protections, mutation controls, or integrity properties of retained chat history.
The artifacts do not say who can access the retained staff chats or what protections apply during the 7 day retention period.
Short chat retention affects provenance and investigation, but the design does not show service outage or workload exhaustion through this store.
The artifacts do not specify transport integrity, request signing, or whether refund parameters can be altered in transit to the processor.
The artifacts do not state whether the processor connection is encrypted or whether sensitive refund payloads are exposed in transit logs.
No batching, retry storm, or unbounded call pattern is described on the processor flow, so denial of service is not evidenced from this edge.

rating.rationale: Present risk is dominated by the missing attributable provenance on irreversible refunds executed with a shared service account. No declared structural or behavioral controls reduce that property finding, and no forecast trigger increases the tier above the present residual in the provided design. Manual validation only; assessment reflects declared design and configuration rather than observed runtime behavior.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.
No tool manifest, source code, or processor API policy was provided, so credential scope and enforcement are assessed from runtime notes only.
No runtime evidence of approval gates, refund thresholds, transport security, or log integrity was provided; absent details were not assumed.
